title: Bilirubin test in newborns
what: This checks the level of bilirubin, the substance that makes a baby's skin look yellow. Often a device is first held to the skin, and blood is taken if needed.
why: For jaundice in a newborn, to see if it will go away on its own or if light therapy is needed.
duration: the skin device takes a few seconds, a blood test a few minutes; results usually come the same day
tell_doctor: How many days old your baby is and if they were born on time
How your baby feeds and how many wet diapers they have a day
The color of the stool and urine
Your blood type and Rh factor, if you know them

prepare.title: Feeding
prepare.text: Feed your baby as usual. No special prep is needed.

prepare.title: Warmth
prepare.text: Put socks on. Blood is easier to take from a warm heel.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes that open easily. The device is held to the forehead or chest.

bring: The referral, if you have one
The discharge papers from the maternity hospital
steps: The nurse holds a device to your baby's forehead or chest
In a second, it shows an approximate level
If an exact level is needed, a drop of blood is taken from the heel or a vein
A cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: Your baby will not feel the device
The prick is quick. Your baby may cry. Breastfeed or cuddle them
after: Results usually come the same day
If bilirubin is high, the doctor may order light therapy, called phototherapy
The test is often repeated in a day or two
red_flags: Your baby is floppy, feeds poorly, or is hard to wake: see a doctor urgently
Jaundice gets worse, or the stool is pale or the urine dark: see a doctor the same day

faq.q: Is jaundice in a newborn dangerous?
faq.a: Most often it is normal and goes away on its own in 1 to 2 weeks. The test makes sure a high level is not missed.
Putting your baby in the sun is not advised. They can overheat or get sunburned. Your doctor will decide on treatment.

reminders.text: Your baby's bilirubin check is soon. Put socks on and bring the maternity hospital discharge papers.
